record.paper_title: Open Questions in High Energy Spin Physics
record.context_brief: Proliferation of distribution and fragmentation functions
record.original_question: Classify, relate, and interpret the expanding set of transverse-momentum-dependent and x-dependent distribution and fragmentation functions introduced for detailed DIS phenomena such as k⊥ distributions, higher twist, and semi-inclusive processes. The open questions are whether these functions are independent or connected by unrecognized symmetries, what physical interpretation fragmentation functions have analogous to the parton model for distributions, whether some functions are unnecessary, and how useful the Wandzura-Wilczek approximation is when it ignores dynamical higher twist.

evidence.quote: Can some deeper order be found in the proliferation of k⊥ and x dependent distribution and fragmentation functions?

In response to new measurements of detailed properties in DIS (k⊥ distributions, higher twist, semi-inclusive processes), theorists have introduced a wonderful new zoo of distribution and fragmentation functions.

Now we need some clever zoology to classify, relate, and interpret these new functions. Are they all independent or are they related to one another by as yet unappreciated symmetries? What is the general physical interpretation of fragmentation functions analogous to the parton model of distribution functions? Perhaps some of them need to become extinct? How useful is the Wandzura-Wilczek approximation, which systematically ignores dynamical higher twist?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the parton-level description of deep-inelastic scattering (DIS) and semi-inclusive DIS (SIDIS) of leptons off hadrons. In the analysis of phenomena involving intrinsic transverse momentum k⊥, higher-twist contributions, and semi-inclusive final states, one introduces a large collection of x-dependent and (x, k⊥)-dependent quark distribution functions (encoding the structure of the target hadron) and fragmentation functions (encoding the hadronization of a struck parton), classified by twist (twist-2, twist-3, twist-4, …), by the polarization of the parent/produced hadron and the parton (unpolarized, longitudinally polarized, transversely polarized, tensor-polarized), and by behavior under time reversal (T-even and T-odd functions, the latter enabled by gauge-link structure).

Address the following:

(a) Provide a complete classification of all independent transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) distribution and fragmentation functions, for hadrons of spin 0, 1/2, and 1, up through twist 4, using Hermiticity, parity, and Lorentz covariance of the quark–quark correlator (without imposing naive time-reversal, so as to include T-odd functions), and determine whether the resulting set is minimal — i.e., whether any of these functions are redundant or whether some of them are linked by previously unrecognized symmetries (discrete, Lorentz, equation-of-motion, or operator-identity relations).

(b) Give a general physical interpretation of fragmentation functions analogous to the probabilistic parton-model interpretation enjoyed by leading-twist distribution functions (number densities of partons of given polarization and transverse momentum inside a hadron).

(c) Determine, quantitatively and qualitatively, the validity and usefulness of the Wandzura–Wilczek approximation — the approximation in which the genuine twist-3 (dynamical quark–gluon–quark correlation) contributions to structure functions and azimuthal/spin asymmetries are dropped and only the Wandzura–Wilczek twist-2 kinematical pieces are kept — across the full set of inclusive and semi-inclusive observables to which the above TMD distribution and fragmentation functions contribute.
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made: complete classifications of TMD distribution and fragmentation functions for spin-1/2 and (more recently) spin-1 hadrons up through twist 4 have been carried out, including T-odd functions and equation-of-motion/Lorentz-invariance relations among them. Wandzura–Wilczek-type approximations have been systematically explored for SIDIS observables. However, the full physical interpretation of higher-twist fragmentation functions and the quantitative validity of the Wandzura–Wilczek approximation across all observables remain active, only partially resolved research topics.

status_evidence.title: Transverse-momentum-dependent parton distribution functions up to twist 4 for spin-1 hadrons
status_evidence.snippet: 40 TMDs exist in the tensor-polarized spin-1 hadron in twists 2–4, obtained by Lorentz-invariant decomposition of the quark correlator under Hermiticity and parity.
status_evidence.claim: Complete classifications of TMDs (including for spin-1 hadrons) up through twist 4 have been carried out.

status_evidence.title: Semi-inclusive deep-inelastic scattering in Wandzura-Wilczek-type approximation
status_evidence.snippet: Systematic study of SIDIS observables in the Wandzura–Wilczek-type approximation neglecting dynamical twist-3 quark-gluon-quark correlations.
status_evidence.claim: Wandzura–Wilczek-type approximations have been systematically tested in SIDIS but their validity remains an active question.

status_evidence.title: Generalized Wandzura–Wilczek Relations and Orbital Angular Momentum
status_evidence.snippet: WW relations express the mismatch between Lorentz-invariant OPE and light-front quantization in higher twist.
status_evidence.claim: Generalized WW relations have been derived, partially clarifying higher-twist structure.

status_evidence.title: Higher Twists (V. M. Braun)
status_evidence.snippet: Review of higher-twist contributions and their phenomenological status.
status_evidence.claim: Higher-twist physics, including the role of dynamical twist-3, remains an active research area.
